svg.title: Five Commercial File Types, One Common Collection Base
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-04-commercial-subniche-fee-yields; chart type: horizontal_bars; title: Five Commercial File Types, One Common Collection Base; subtitle: Compare illustrative service-fee yield per $100,000 actually recovered.; chapter number: 2; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: All five bars assume $100,000 in cleared recoveries and show gross operator fee yield before expenses. Rates are editorial pricing hypotheses, not observed market rates or recovery probabilities. Bars are alternatives, not additive revenue.; caption: Use a common recovered-dollar denominator to compare pricing. Neither the debtor's asset value nor the judgment balance establishes earned revenue.; stages: label: Document-complete supplier judgments; value: $100,000 recovered at 20% produces $20,000 service-fee revenue; numeric value: 20000.0; detail: Assume an entered trade-credit judgment and voluntary payment using bank-supported business ACH or wire transfer. Confirm payment authority, return exposure, and ledger allocation; a convenient rail does not improve lien priority.; label: Equipment lease deficiency judgments; value: $100,000 recovered at 25% produces $25,000 service-fee revenue; numeric value: 25000.0; detail: Assume a valid commercial deficiency judgment after credited disposition proceeds. Counsel reviews remaining liability and secured claims before selecting a recovery route; prevent double recovery.; label: Commercial premises rent judgments; value: $100,000 recovered at 25% produces $25,000 service-fee revenue; numeric value: 25000.0; detail: Confirm the named tenant entity, judgment scope, credited deposits, and any adjudicated guarantor liability. Separate commercial obligations from household-purpose debts and verify assets belong to an actual judgment debtor.; label: Adjudicated business guarantor obligations; value: $100,000 recovered at 30% produces $30,000 service-fee revenue; numeric value: 30000.0; detail: Assume judgment already reaches the guarantor. Classify the underlying obligation by purpose, not the person's name; counsel evaluates ownership, exemptions, and available execution procedure.; label: Lien-constrained commercial judgments; value: $100,000 recovered at 35% produces $35,000 service-fee revenue; numeric value: 35000.0; detail: Higher assumed pricing reflects more intensive priority and asset analysis, not superior collectability. Senior claims can eliminate reachable equity; decline further spend when incremental recovery economics fail.

text.title: Five Commercial File Types, One Common Collection Base
text.tspan: Five Commercial File Types, One Common Collection Base

rect.title: label: Document-complete supplier judgments; value: $100,000 recovered at 20% produces $20,000 service-fee revenue; numeric value: 20000.0; detail: Assume an entered trade-credit judgment and voluntary payment using bank-supported business ACH or wire transfer. Confirm payment authority, return exposure, and ledger allocation; a convenient rail does not improve lien priority.

label: Equipment lease deficiency judgments; value: $100,000 recovered at 25% produces $25,000 service-fee revenue; numeric value: 25000.0; detail: Assume a valid commercial deficiency judgment after credited disposition proceeds. Counsel reviews remaining liability and secured claims before selecting a recovery route; prevent double recovery.

label: Commercial premises rent judgments; value: $100,000 recovered at 25% produces $25,000 service-fee revenue; numeric value: 25000.0; detail: Confirm the named tenant entity, judgment scope, credited deposits, and any adjudicated guarantor liability. Separate commercial obligations from household-purpose debts and verify assets belong to an actual judgment debtor.

label: Adjudicated business guarantor obligations; value: $100,000 recovered at 30% produces $30,000 service-fee revenue; numeric value: 30000.0; detail: Assume judgment already reaches the guarantor. Classify the underlying obligation by purpose, not the person's name; counsel evaluates ownership, exemptions, and available execution procedure.

label: Lien-constrained commercial judgments; value: $100,000 recovered at 35% produces $35,000 service-fee revenue; numeric value: 35000.0; detail: Higher assumed pricing reflects more intensive priority and asset analysis, not superior collectability. Senior claims can eliminate reachable equity; decline further spend when incremental recovery economics fail.

text.title: Assumptions: All five bars assume $100,000 in cleared recoveries and show gross operator fee yield before expenses. Rates are editorial pricing hypotheses, not observed market rates or recovery probabilities. Bars are alternatives, not additive revenue.
